text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Malaysia was deeply concerned that its ambassador to Peru, Ahmad Mokhtar Selat, was among the 140 still held by Marxist rebels in Lima, a Foreign Ministry statement said. It said Malaysia would continue its efforts to secure the early release of Ahmad Mokhtar.

-- Malaysian corporate figure Mohd Nadzmi Mohd Salleh denied that the company he formed to take over state-owned Mara Holdings Sdn Bhd has any Singapore link. He was commenting on a news report that the company, Trisico Folec, which is to take Mara has a Singaporean stake.
-- Massive traffic jams were reported in Kuala Lumpur on Monday and police said the problem was mainly due to the last minute rush of Christmas shoppers.
